name: MonarchAiScore
title: AiScore
wrapsNative: MonarchScoreRing (ProgressView with a ring style) or a Capsule bar, MonarchBadge for the band, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, and a DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) for the band legend
summary: A 0 to 100 score produced by a model, as a ring or a bar, with its band, the rationale and the factors that raised or lowered it.
whenToUse: To show a model's score for a record, such as a lead, churn or fit score, with the reasons behind it.
whenNotToUse: Not for a score a person or a rule computed (use MonarchScoreRing) and not for how sure the model is of an answer (use MonarchAiConfidenceMeter).
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, value: Double?, bands: [MonarchAiScoreBand] = MonarchAiScoreBand.defaults, rationale: String? = nil, factors: [MonarchAiScoreFactor] = [], variant: MonarchAiScoreVariant = .ring, size: MonarchAiScoreSize = .md, showsBands: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiScoreLabels = MonarchAiScoreLabels())
struct MonarchAiScoreBand { init(minimum: Double, label: String, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral); static var defaults: [MonarchAiScoreBand] }
struct MonarchAiScoreFactor { init(_ label: String, impact: Double, detail: String? = nil) }

struct MonarchAiScoreLabels { init(label: String? = nil, aiGenerated: String? = nil, valueText: ((String, String) -> String)? = nil, unavailable: String? = nil, factors: String? = nil, impact: ((String, Bool) -> String)? = nil, noImpact: String? = nil, bands: String? = nil, currentBand: String? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: What is scored, such as "Lead score". "Score" when nil.

options.name: value
options.description: The score from 0 to 100; values outside are limited. nil while there is no score.

options.name: bands
options.description: Named ranges with a minimum, a label and a MonarchTone. Low (0, danger), Medium (40, warning) and High (70, success) by default.

options.name: rationale
options.description: Why the model gave this score, in plain words.

options.name: factors
options.description: The inputs that moved the score, each with a label, a signed impact and an optional detail.

options.name: variant
options.description: A ring with the number in its centre, or a bar with the number above it.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the ring: sm or md.

options.name: showsBands
options.description: Whether the band legend disclosure is offered.

states.name: scored
states.description: The ring or bar fills to the score in the band's tone; the band badge shows the tone's icon and the band's name.

states.name: no score
states.description: An empty ring with a dash, or "No score yet" above an empty bar; no band badge.

states.name: factors
states.description: Each factor shows its label, detail, a signed impact with an up or down arrow and a small bar sized against the largest impact.

states.name: legend
states.description: A collapsed disclosure, "How to read this score", listing each band with a swatch and its range; the current band is marked "(this score)" in bold.

appearance: The ring is a MonarchScoreRing in the band's tone; the bar fill and the legend swatches use the tone's solid role on the muted background track; raised and lowered impacts use the success and danger strong roles; text uses the default and muted text roles. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web lists factors and bands in tables; iOS shows rows, each read as one element. The web's tones include ai and info; MonarchTone has no ai case, so a band cannot take the AI colour on iOS. The web's locale prop is the SwiftUI locale environment. label, rationale and factor text are plain strings on iOS, not arbitrary content.
accessibility: The ring is one element named by the label, with the value "72 out of 100" or "No score yet"; the band badge is read after it.
The bar is one element named by the label, with the value "72 out of 100, High".
The band is always written and shown with the tone's icon, so it never depends on colour.
Each factor is one element: its label, then "Raised the score by 18" or "Lowered the score by 9" and its detail.
The legend is the Monarch disclosure button; each band row is read as one element and the current band is marked in words.
Headings (the label and the factors heading) have the header trait; text scales with Dynamic Type and the header stacks when it does not fit.
edgeCases: Scores above 100 or below 0 are limited; NaN counts as no score.
A score below the lowest band's minimum takes the lowest band.
Band upper bounds are the next band's minimum minus one, and 100 for the last.
Impacts are compared with the largest impact, and never with less than 1 point.

examples.title: Ring with rationale and factors
examples.template:
MonarchAiScore(
    {{label}},
    value: {{value|double}},
    rationale: {{rationale}},
    factors: [
        MonarchAiScoreFactor({{factors.0.label}}, impact: {{factors.0.impact|double}}, detail: {{factors.0.detail}}),
        MonarchAiScoreFactor({{factors.1.label}}, impact: {{factors.1.impact|double}}),
        MonarchAiScoreFactor({{factors.2.label}}, impact: {{factors.2.impact|double}}),
        MonarchAiScoreFactor({{factors.3.label}}, impact: {{factors.3.impact|double}}, detail: {{factors.3.detail}}),
    ]
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiScore(
    "Lead score",
    value: 72.0,
    rationale: "Engaged with recent emails and pricing, but no meeting is booked yet.",
    factors: [
        MonarchAiScoreFactor("Opened the last three emails", impact: 14.0, detail: "All within the past week"),
        MonarchAiScoreFactor("Visited the pricing page", impact: 9.0),
        MonarchAiScoreFactor("No meeting booked yet", impact: -11.0),
        MonarchAiScoreFactor("Company size", impact: 0.0, detail: "Within the usual range"),
    ]
)

examples.title: A bar with custom bands
examples.code:
MonarchAiScore(
    "Match",
    value: 58,
    bands: [
        MonarchAiScoreBand(minimum: 0, label: "Weak", tone: .neutral),
        MonarchAiScoreBand(minimum: 50, label: "Strong", tone: .info),
    ],
    variant: .bar
)
